text:
Colorado out-chanced Toronto 4.64 to 3.07 in expected goals, attempted 78 shots to the Leafs' 43, and won the simulated replay of this game 84 percent of the time. Toronto won 6-3 anyway. Mackenzie Blackwood let in five goals on 22 shots, 2.77 more than the chances against him warranted, while Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 of 33 and saved 1.64 goals above expectation.

The second period was where the gap opened widest. Colorado generated 2.09 expected goals to Toronto's 0.61, and Brock Nelson's snap shot, a 35 percent chance, put the Avalanche up 3-2. Gabriel Landeskog then had a 25 percent look that Bobrovsky turned away. Instead of extending the lead, Colorado watched William Nylander tie it at 16:47 on a 12 percent chance, and Easton Cowan scored 46 seconds later on an 8 percent slap shot to make it 4-3. Nathan MacKinnon had scored twice in the first on chances of 7 and 6 percent, so the low-percentage shots had gone both ways.

Special teams finished it. Toronto went 2 for 4 on the power play despite only 0.46 expected goals, with Nylander and Auston Matthews both cashing in. Colorado went 0 for 5 on 1.35 expected goals. Matthews added an empty look at 19:21 on a 62 percent chance for the sixth goal. Nylander finished with two goals and three assists, and Matthews two and two, as Toronto turned a night of being outplayed into a three-goal win.
